pamphlet_excerpts: Paint Two Different Surfaces Using: Prepare and paint two different surfaces: Applying primer, the first coat of paint, also is the last stage ofsurface preparation (p. 51).

Paint Two Different Surfaces Using Principle 2: Prepare and paint two different surfaces Principle 2: The primer makes the next coat stick to thesurface, protects the substrate, and seals the surface (p. 51).

Paint Two Different Surfaces Using Principle 3: Prepare and paint two different surfaces Principle 3: There aredifferent primers for wood, concrete and masonry, plaster anddrywall, steel, and other metals (p. 51).

Paint Two Different Surfaces Using Principle 4: Prepare and paint two different surfaces Principle 4: Wood primers are available in oil-based or water-based products and can be used indoors or outdoors (p. 51).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Paint Two Different Surfaces Using): Step 1 (Prepare and paint two different surfaces): Exterior masonry surfaces are often highly alkaline, so be sure to use primers on surfaces that are alkali-resistant (p. 51).

Step 2 (Paint Two Different Surfaces Using): Step 2 (Prepare and paint two different surfaces): Make sure primers for plaster surfaces are alkali-resistant and that plaster dust is removedfirst (p. 51).
Step 3 (Paint Two Different Surfaces Using): Step 3 (Prepare and paint two different surfaces): The best primers for drywall or gypsum board are waterbased, such as vinyl and acrylic (p. 51).

Step 4 (Paint Two Different Surfaces Using): Step 4 (Prepare and paint two different surfaces): The type of primer you choose depends on the surface preparation required as well as the topcoat to beapplied over the primer (p. 51).
